Fixed `applyDiscount` in `src/price.js`.

**Cause:** It subtracted the percentage directly from the paise amount (`paise - percent`) instead of calculating a percentage of the price.

**Fix:**
```js
export function applyDiscount(paise, percent) {
  return paise - Math.floor((paise * percent) / 100)
}
```

The discount is rounded down to the nearest paise, matching the test expectations (e.g., 999 at 10% → 99 paise off → 900).

**Verified:** `node --test` passes — 1 test, 1 pass, 0 fail.

broader set programmatically against an independent reference? Let me spot-check a few.
`parseDate` is implemented in `src/date.js` and all 7 tests pass (the original three cases plus the ones I added).

**Approach:**
- The text is `trim()`ed, then matched against exactly three anchored patterns. There is no `Date` anywhere: everything is done with regex groups plus `Number()` and a hand-written days-per-month table.
  - `^(\d{1,2}) ([A-Za-z]+) (\d{4})$` — day, month name, year
  - `^(\d{2})([-/])(\d{2})\2(\d{4})$` — day-first; the backreference forces the two separators to match, so `05-11/2026` is rejected
  - `^(\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2})$` — ISO order, checked before the day-first pattern
- Month names match only on full name or first-three letters, case-insensitively (`monthFromName`), so "Nov", "NOV", "november" work and "Sept" or "Novem" don't.
- **Error split:** a structural match with a bad value throws `RangeError` (`month < 1 || month > 12`, or `day < 1 || day > daysInMonth`); anything that fails to match, including an unknown month name, throws a plain `Error`. Unknown name is signalled by `null` rather than `0` so it can't be confused with a numeric month `00` — my first run caught that exact bug (`2026-00-10` was throwing a plain `Error`).
- Gregorian leap rule: `y % 4 === 0 && (y % 100 !== 0 || y % 400 === 0)` — 2024/2000/2400 are leap; 1900/2026/2100 are not.

Verified behaviours: `31/04/2026`, `29 Feb 2026`, `29 Feb 1900`, `2026-13-01`, `00/01/2026`, `0 Dec 2026`, `2026-11-00` all throw `RangeError`; `Novem`, `5 Novem 2026`, `5/11/26`, `05.11.2026`, `5-Nov-2026`, `2026-2-3`, `5  Nov 2026` (double internal space), empty string and non-strings all throw plain `Error`.

Two judgement calls where the spec is silent, worth flagging: internal whitespace in the name form must be single spaces (only *surrounding* whitespace is ignored, per your wording), and any 4-digit year including `0000` is accepted since only day and month are specified as range-checked.
